name: go-workflows-durable-worker-run-outcomes
instr:
go-workflows cannot currently expose durable worker run outcomes for observing, snapshotting, and awaiting asynchronous workflow and activity results. Add reporting that preserves meaningful identity and failure evidence across polling, execution, persistence, shutdown, composite workers, and orchestration without changing legacy lifecycle behavior.

Export all public outcome symbols from `github.com/cschleiden/go-workflows/worker`. Failures retain their original error, task identity, lifecycle phase, and disposition. `TaskKind` starts with `iota`: `TaskKindWorkflow`, then `TaskKindActivity`. `FailurePhase` starts with `iota`: `FailurePhaseStart`, `FailurePhasePoll`, `FailurePhaseQueue`, `FailurePhaseHeartbeat`, `FailurePhaseExecute`, `FailurePhaseCache`, then `FailurePhaseComplete`. `TaskDisposition` starts with `iota`: `TaskDispositionCompleted`, `TaskDispositionFailed`, `TaskDispositionOwnershipLost`, then `TaskDispositionAbandoned`. `FailurePolicy` starts with `iota`: `FailurePolicyContinue`, then `FailurePolicyStop`.

Give every accepted task exactly one terminal disposition. Polling failures create no accepted work and consume no reservations. Continue policy resumes polling; stop policy does not; both drain accepted work. Heartbeat extension failure records lost ownership, cancels execution, suppresses backend completion, and produces exactly one ownership-lost outcome despite races.

Distinguish invocation, execution, conversion, cache, lease, and durable completion e
